properties.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor Parcel blklot 8722025 (Mission Bay South Blocks 29-32), with the two Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4 office-tower footprints (real OpenStreetMap building outlines, OSM ways 1410182008 and 1410183655) subtracted out -- see digitization_method.
properties.digitization_method: ADDED (as status.csv row, blklot 8722025): Chase Center promoted from an orientation-only landmark to a tracked record. MIGRATED 2026-09-23 from status.csv to this hand-derived geometry, per the owner's direct instruction: DataSF's own Assessor Parcel dataset gives blklot 8722025 (Chase Center) and blklot 8722063 (Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4, the two office towers) byte-identical geometry -- the same shared underlying master-condominium-association land parcel spanning the whole Blocks 29-32 superblock (confirmed: Chase Center, both Uber towers, a parking structure and a small broadcast building are all separate condo units on one shared plat, per a CommercialCafe report on the site's financing). Joining Chase Center to that parcel directly made it visually indistinguishable from the Uber towers on the map (identical overlapping polygons; a click on the shared area could resolve to either record). This geometry instead traces what's real and excludes what's real-but-not-Chase-Center: it is the full Assessor parcel (blklot 8722025, 44,178 sqm) with the two Uber towers' own real building footprints (traced from OpenStreetMap, OSM ways 1410182008 '1655 3rd St / Uber Headquarters Building 3' and 1410183655 '1725 3rd St / Uber Headquarters Building 4', combined ~8,732 sqm) subtracted out via shapely.difference(). The remainder (~35,532 sqm) is the arena bowl, its surrounding plaza/Thrive City retail, and the small satellite structures around it -- including Harmonic Brewing's own standalone taproom building at the NE edge (7 Warriors Way Ste 206), confirmed via its own DataSF business-registration address and geocoded location, which the owner directed be folded into this record rather than tracked separately. Verified the arena's own roofline (visible in Esri satellite imagery) falls entirely within the resulting polygon before accepting the subtraction.
properties.accuracy_caveat: REAL, DERIVED BOUNDARY -- the outer edge is a real DataSF Assessor Parcel boundary (blklot 8722025); the two notches cut into its NW and SW corners are real OpenStreetMap building traces (the Uber towers), not estimates. The resulting shape has not been independently verified against a surveyed Chase Center site plan -- it is real-minus-real, not a single authoritative source. Two small structures inside this polygon (an oval building in the west plaza, and possibly others) remain unidentified as of this pass. street_clip_exempt is set: the real-street centerline layer (src/street_geometry.py) shows several stale/closed street segments cutting straight through the arena bowl itself (visible as a literal cross running under the roof in a direct render against the street buffer) -- leftover records from the four separate plan blocks (29/30/31/32) that were consolidated into one superblock when Chase Center was built, not real current streets. Auto-clipping against them removed 16% of this polygon's real area; exempted per the same documented-reason precedent as Pier 70's 20th Street Plaza.
properties.notes: OCII/Warriors Mission Bay South Blocks 29-32. 1 Warriors Way; DataSF's own roll also lists 7 Warriors Way and 300 16th St for pieces of this same parcel. Anchors an 11-acre mixed-use development including Thrive City retail (~100,000 sq ft) and a 35,000 sq ft public plaza. Designed by MANICA Architecture (interiors by Gensler); privately financed (~$1.4B) by Warriors ownership. Opened Sept 6, 2019.
